hypotheses_validated.claim: Verifier finding (major) reproduced and fixed: decode no longer collapses as n_threads approaches the logical CPU count. Root cause: every region waits for all workers (hx_pool_run), model.c dispatched even tiny regions, and with 1000 us worker spins a descheduled worker or caller costs about one spin period per region once threads + other load exceed the logical CPUs. Fix in model.c: (1) POOL_SPIN_US 1000 -> 50; (2) par_for(): a region runs on the caller when its estimated single-thread work is below PAR_MIN_NS = 6 us (per-site estimates, calibrated with an instrumented build: GQA scores/softmax at short context, tiny models' matmuls, etc.); (3) two pools: batches under SMT_MIN_T = 256 tokens run on min(n_threads, physical cores) threads, larger ones on n_threads (SMT helps only large prefill batches); api.c caps n_threads at the logical CPUs (warning) and logs when SMT threads are requested.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: hearth-bench, synthetic Qwen3-30B-A3B-shaped Q4 container (17.0 GB), --cache-gb 20 --prompt 16 --warmup 48 --tokens 48, 9950X, other engineers' load 29-38%: gen-001 build 16 thr 20.6-23.7 tok/s, 32 thr 2.07-2.14 tok/s (reproduced, 467-483 ms/token); gen-002 build 8/16/24/28/32 thr = 19.8-22.2 / 19.8-22.0 / 21.1-21.9 / 20.9-21.4 / 19.8-21.3 tok/s (3 sweeps). Tiny 64-expert Q4 model (make_tiny n_layers 4, E 64, top-6), --max-batch 1 decode: gen-001 1/4/16/32 thr 14677/14061/12549/29.7 tok/s, gen-002 14009/16367/14081/13995 tok/s. Spin sweep (every region on the pool, same container): 1000 us 23.7/22.7/2.1, 200 us 22.3/18.4/7.3, 100 us 21.6/19.8/10.4, 50 us 23.4/22.5/14.2, 0 us 16.5/14.7/13.0 tok/s at 16/24/32 threads. Prefill (warm cache, T=512): 16 thr 395 tok/s, 32 thr 438 tok/s (SMT pool). Output bit-identical across all of these (test_model, golden suite).

hypotheses_validated.claim: Regression tests for the major finding: test_overhead checks by count that a tiny model's decode runs zero regions on the pool at n_threads = logical CPUs (seam hx_model_regions) and that the forced-parallel threshold does run regions, plus a generous timing bound (best of 3, 4x + 20 ms vs 1 thread); every engine opened by the tests forces regions onto the pool (seam hx_model_set_parallel_min(m, 0)) except configurations marked 'default scheduling', so INV-DET-1/2 still exercise the parallel paths; test_long runs a 300-token batch with n_threads = physical cores + 2 (SMT pool) followed by decode-sized calls on the per-core pool.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: A copy of model.c with PAR_MIN_NS 0 fails test_overhead ('a tiny model's decode ran 2248 regions on the pool'). On a quiet machine the timing bound alone did not fail with the old scheduling (1.52 ms vs 0.62 ms for 40 tokens), which is why the count check exists; only a loaded machine shows the cliff.

hypotheses_validated.claim: Finding (minor) LFU heat / usage_out under-count in batched eval: fixed within the existing hx_store contract. After a wave, model.c calls hx_store_try_acquire + hx_store_release (u_n[u] - 1) more times per expert (guaranteed hits: the slab is still held), so the store counts one use per (token, rank). Per-expert heat, usage_out and cache hits + misses (= expert_uses) are now identical for one batch, chunks of 5 and token-by-token evaluation; batched hit rates are per activation, matching hearth.sim's hit_rate definition.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: test_usage_counts (heat arrays memcmp-equal across the three schedules, sum = expert_uses = 48; hits + misses = uses); the mutant without the loop fails 4 checks. Hearth-bench prefill 32 tokens, 4 GiB cache: 'hit 68.5%' (per activation) vs gen-001's '2.1%' (per unique expert). Cost: ~1.5% of fully cached 512-token prefill (387.8 vs 381.5 / 382.8 tok/s with and without the loop, 2 runs each); a store-side counter would remove it (contract_issues).

hypotheses_validated.claim: Finding (minor) failed multi-chunk eval: fixed. hx_model_eval buffers the call's routing rows (tpend, grown to n * n_moe * top_k * 2 bytes only while tracing; written once when every chunk succeeded) and restores tokens / forward_calls / expert_uses / expert_loads_unique on failure; time counters and store statistics keep the attempt (documented in hx_model.h).

hypotheses_validated.claim: Finding (minor) trace_start with an unopenable path stopped the active trace: fixed (the new file is opened and its header written before the old trace is closed; restarting the same path truncates and restarts it).

hypotheses_validated.claim: Finding (minor) replay ignores n_layers: resolved by requiring n_layers >= n_moe_layers (header consistency, as hearth.sim.trace's loader requires) and documenting that n_layers is otherwise not compared. A strict n_layers == L check would reject hearth.sim.trace.synthetic(...) traces made without n_layers (they carry n_layers = n_moe_layers) on models with leading dense layers (DeepSeek-V3 / Kimi-K2 shapes), and replay needs only the MoE geometry.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: python/hearth/sim/trace.py: synthetic(..., n_layers=0) -> Trace(..., n_layers or L) with L = n_moe_layers. test_invariants: n_layers = n_moe_layers - 1 and version 2 rejected; n_layers = n_moe_layers and 1000 accepted; a rejected file leaves the active replay running (same logits as before the rejection).

hypotheses_falsified.claim: A wall-clock perf smoke test (many threads vs one thread on a tiny model) catches the scheduling regression.
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: On a quiet machine the old scheduling (every region on the pool, 1000 us spin) was only 2.5x slower at 32 threads (1.52 vs 0.62 ms per 40 tokens), inside any bound loose enough not to flake; the 100x cliff needs external load. Replaced the primary check by a deterministic region count (hx_model_regions); the timing bound is kept as a secondary smoke check.

hypotheses_falsified.claim: A short worker spin costs nothing anywhere.
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: 4 GiB cache, direct I/O, replayed Zipf trace, 16 threads, 2 runs each: spin 50 us 13.47/13.44, 250 us 13.51/13.56, 1000 us 13.72/13.80 tok/s (workers sleep during I/O waits and must be woken per wave). Kept 50 us: the cost is ~2% in the I/O-bound case versus up to 10x under oversubscription; a yielding spin in pool.c would remove the trade-off (contract_issues).

open_questions: Prefill at 16 threads measured 376-383 tok/s vs gen-001's 390-412 in back-to-back runs on a loaded machine; ~1.5% is the per-activation use counting (measured), the rest is within run-to-run noise but was not conclusively attributed. Re-measure on a quiet machine (T09).
PAR_MIN_NS (6 us) and the per-site ns estimates were calibrated on this Zen 5 CPU with one instrumented build; other CPUs may prefer other thresholds. Output never depends on them.
SMT_MIN_T = 256 comes from one prefill sweep (T=64/128/256/512 at 16 vs 32 threads); speculative-decoding batch sizes (4-16) clearly belong to the per-core pool, the 128-256 range is a wash.

Open questions carried from gen-001 that this generation did not address: prefetch precision on real routing, F16/BF16 KV cache, an AVX-512 canonical axpy for the attention value pass (single-thread GQA value pass is ~6x slower per MAC than the score pass: 43.8 vs 7.3 us per layer at ~75 positions), DeepSeek/Kimi-shaped MLA benchmarks.
